text: 🇲🇽🌎 "We have a free trade agreement with the United States, we don't have one with China, but we have a lot of trade with China. So we want to export more to China." "Imports, not only from China, from various countries, reduced the productive capacity of several sectors in the country. And our interest is that more is produced in Mexico." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, Nov 25, 2026 Correcting a reporter, Sheinbaum said there were no agreements at her meeting with Xi Jinping in Shenzhen: "a very good meeting, with a lot of communication, frank dialogue." Economy Secretary Marcelo Ebrard then met his Chinese counterpart about opening China to more Mexican exports, from agricultural products up, and a working group is being set up. China's CRRC is already building the México–Pachuca trains in Ciudad Sahagún. On the trip, she said, Mexico sought to convey "republican austerity, honesty and love for the people."
banner: CHINA: EXPORT MORE, PRODUCE MORE AT HOME

text: 🇲🇽🛢️ "Today regular gasoline is at 24 pesos, a little under 24 pesos, 23.99. But if we hadn't made this agreement, that liter of gasoline would have reached 30, 32 pesos." "The United States has a problem, Europe has an inflation problem, and we have been able to contain it." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, Nov 25, 2026 Inflation came in at 3.96%. Sheinbaum said her government received it at around 4.7% in October 2024, and 3.96% "is not high inflation." She credited two voluntary agreements: one with gas station owners that holds fuel prices down, and the PACIC basket of staple products capped at 911 pesos. Without the fuel deal, diesel, now just under 27 pesos, would have reached 35. She also showed that Mexico ranks fifth in the world for foreign direct investment, with 43 billion dollars.

🇲🇽🎨 "The transformation of Mexico also happens in how we relate to one another. Men have a lot to do, to recognize, to question and to change." — María Elvira Concheiro, Undersecretary for Substantive Equality, Mañanera, Nov 25, 2026 Mexico launched "Hombres por la Transformación," a national campaign built on 12 commitments drafted in working groups with men from different sectors. More than 500 CONALEP students in Iztapalapa signed them live during the mañanera. The campaign will reach more than 300 CONALEP campuses and some 170,000 students, and then the whole Bachillerato Nacional. The commitments include renouncing "any complicity that tolerates machismo, classism and racism," rejecting online groups that spread extreme hatred and humiliation of women among young men, sharing care work, and conceiving "power as service (...) and not as a form of oppression."

🇲🇽✊ "We are talking about 20 million women who receive support from the government of Mexico." "Zero impunity for sexual abuse, zero impunity for any kind of violence against women." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, Nov 25, 2026 On the International Day for the Elimination of Violence against Women, Sheinbaum counted the Women's Well-being pension (about 3 million women aged 60–64), the older-adult pension (about 7 million women), the Rita Cetina, Benito Juárez and Gertrudis Bocanegra scholarships, Jóvenes Escribiendo el Futuro and the working mothers program. With housing and the Centros LIBRE, the reach is at least 27 million women. She described two pillars: attending to the causes, "eradicating machismo from education," and zero impunity. The Women's Secretariat reported 1,001 Centros LIBRE in all 32 states, more than 650,000 women served, and a daily femicide average down a little over 5% from January to August. 500 more centers are planned for 2027.

🇲🇽🏭 <u>Yokohama Opens Its Biggest Plant in the World, in Coahuila</u>

Japan's Yokohama Rubber opened its tire plant in Derramadero, Saltillo, and announced a second phase. Across both, it is investing about 10 billion pesos for more than 1,500 direct jobs, making it Yokohama's largest plant anywhere, El Economista reports. CEO Masataka Yamaishi credited Saltillo's continuous rail and highway links to the US and its skilled workforce. Coahuila says 222 companies from 19 countries arrived in three years, bringing about 190 billion pesos and 86,000 jobs.
banner: YOKOHAMA: BIGGEST PLANT ON EARTH, COAHUILA

text:
🇲🇽☕ <u>Sheinbaum to Nestlé: Pay Chiapas Coffee Growers a Fair Price</u>

Coffee growers protesting in Tapachula say intermediaries pay them 43 pesos per kilo, and they're asking Nestlé for 50 to 60. They say some 165,000 families depend on the crop. Sheinbaum sided with them: she ordered the Agriculture ministry to join the negotiations, asked Nestlé to buy directly with no middlemen, and asked why the price of finished products like Nescafé never falls in the same proportion. In October, Nestlé pledged to double its Mexico investment to US$2 billion by 2030, with coffee at the center.

🇲🇽⚖️ <u>Mexico City Bets 400 Million Pesos on Prisons That Rehabilitate</u>

Mexico City is launching a Humanist Penitentiary Model and the "Alas de Colibrí" program (Autonomy, Freedom, Accompaniment and Second Chances), with 400 million pesos in 2027 to rebuild its prisons. Schooling through high school, free university courses with public universities, job training with companies, mental health care, and support after release. Clara Brugada: "A society is not more just for having more prisons, nor safer simply for having more people locked up."

🇲🇽🏥 <u>IMSS-Bienestar: 117,000 Health Workers Get Formal Posts on January 1</u>

More than 117,000 health workers will hold a formal position at IMSS-Bienestar from January 1, 2027, with payroll ready December 15, director Alejandro Svarch reported from Toluca, where he opened the agency's first comprehensive kidney-care center. 1,973 new health professionals were hired in the last two weeks alone. "Todo en tu Clínica" has grown from 3,000 to 5,588 health centers in 21 states, with internet, electronic records, digital pharmacy control and free lab tests.

🇲🇽🌎 <u>Sheinbaum: Cartels Are Not Terrorists, and No Treaty Outranks Our Constitution</u>

Fourteen TIAR members voted at the OAS to convene the Cold War-era treaty against "transnational organized crime." Mexico didn't vote: it left the TIAR in 2002. Sheinbaum backed Ambassador Alejandro Encinas and said her government does not share Washington's push to equate organized crime with terrorism, a label that can be used to justify foreign intervention. Asked whether the treaty could be turned against Mexico: "It shouldn't, because it is not above our Constitution."

🚨🇲🇽 <u>Update: Mexico Left Off Trump's New Tariff List, For Now</u>

The Section 301 "overcapacity" probe covered 16 trading partners. The final USTR proposal targets 14, and Mexico isn't one of them (Norway was also spared). China gets the highest rate; the EU, Japan and India are on the list. The investigation into Mexico stays open: USTR says talks with the Mexican government on Chinese inputs continue, and Jamieson Greer gave no date to close it. The new duties still face public consultation and could take effect only in January 2027.
banner: TRUMP TARIFFS: MEXICO SPARED, FOR NOW
